Households by UK-wide £5,000 band of baseline household net income in 2027-28 (income_basis_year 2027) and income change band (contract change_edges: an exact-zero band from -£1 to £1, edges at ±1, 10, 25, 50, 75, 100, 150, 200, 300, 400, 500, 750, 1,000, 1,500, 2,000, 3,000 and 5,000, open beyond ±£5,000), by measure, package and year (2027-2031), from generate --only household_scatter on Microcosm UK 2024-25 national build microcosm-uk-2024-25-national-20261019T083323Z-6cba5d71 (policyengine 6.10.2, policyengine-uk 2.132.6). Every year's households are banded by their 2027-28 baseline income, so an income band holds the same households in each year and each year's cells count them at that year's weight; year-to-year differences within a band are the uprating of its households' weights plus the weights of households that changed change band, covered by the same floor and rounding as differences between cells. No household rows: cells with fewer than 10 distinct survey households (source_household_id) are left out and counts are rounded to the nearest 1,000. Percentiles (1st to 99th) of equivalised household net income, person-weighted, before and after each measure and the combined run, by year (2026-2031), from generate --only income_distribution --backend modal on the bundle's Microcosm UK 2024-25 dataset (policyengine 6.10.2, policyengine-uk 2.132.6). Income is household net income as the household calculator counts it (household_net_income less public spending in kind on the NHS, schools and transport subsidies, plus the business rates and stamp duty the model attributes to households), divided by the HBAI modified OECD scale; it differs from HBAI income (the decile charts and the Pre-measures forecast's median) mainly by including fuel duty and VAT. Each side is ranked against its own distribution. Each point is the mean income of the people in a band one percentile wide, never one household's figure; a band with fewer than 100 survey households has no row (none was dropped). No ids, weights or counts. No area below the UK. On the nine candidate Autumn Budget 2026 measures and their combined run (candidates modelled before the Budget, not announced policy). Every row is new and awaits review; read by the Household impact tab's 'Where you sit in the UK income distribution' card. Reviewed and signed by Vahid Ahmadi on 26 October 2026, covering these bytes.
